scenario.title: Lakeside Water — billing dispute surge (Mock #6, not an official contest problem)
scenario.description: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled in August-September. Customer Service wants an AI agent. Field reading is contracted out; AMI meters and the meter data management system (MDMS) are run by a vendor.
scenario.initial_request: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

potential_bias: frames the issue as a response-speed problem

interpretation_history.interpretation: Dispute volumes rose from about 610 in June and 590 in July to 1,180 in August and 1,260 in September, showing a roughly two‑fold increase starting in August.
The observation shows that dispute tickets are being answered within a median of 1.6 days and 90th percentile of 2.8 days, both under the 3‑day SLA, with a total of 2,440 tickets recorded.

The observation shows that disputed bills are more frequently associated with ACTUAL meter reads (1785) than ESTIMATED reads (1240), indicating that the dispute increase is not driven primarily by estimation substitution.
No tariff change records were found in the billing system, indicating that tariff changes are not a source of the billing errors driving the dispute increase.
Route completion for August‑September is 0.88, below the target 0.95, indicating a gap in manual meter read execution.
